paragraphs: Asur lilvot sea bisa kol sheen lo lalloveh kelal veen shaar qatzub bashshuq lemin zeh veasur lelavvoto apillu leshaa deshemma yityaqqer hashshaar miyyad ella im ken osehu damim alayv kepi mah sheshshaveh beshaa shemmalvehu veim lo asahu damim venityaqqeru noten lo haddamim shehayu shavim bishat halvaa veim huzelu noten lo hassea shehilvahu velaken otam shelevim zeh mizzeh sea chittim kede liproa achar shabua o yoter asur dechittim en lahem shaar yadua bashshuq beirenu veshumatan ola veyoredet tamid veshemma tityaqqer hassea veissur zeh noheg bekol happerot ki bekol happerot yesh bahem yoqer vezol ella im ken malvehu dabar muat shei derek bene adam lehaqpid al yaquru vezolo kegon kikkar lach shehaishsha lava mechabertah shello hechmiru za"l ledaqdeq beissur ribbit derabbanan kol kak veotam baale battim sheddarkam lilvat zeh mizzeh mine mezonot sheqqorin bearbe grdy"q (reqiqim) esrim o yoter bebat achat yesh leesor dei zeh chashib dabar muat:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to lend "se'ah for se'ah" — that is, to lend a quantity of grain or fruit in order to receive back the same quantity of the same kind — when the borrower has none at all of that kind, and there is no fixed, known market price for that product. The prohibition applies even to a short-term loan, since there is concern the price might rise in the meantime, resulting in the borrower returning more value than he received — which is considered interest. The solution: assess the quantity's monetary value at the time of the loan, so that if the price rises, the borrower returns the money assessed at the outset, and if the price falls, he may return the same quantity in kind. In the Ben Ish Chai's city, wheat had no fixed price, so it was forbidden to lend and receive back se'ah for se'ah without setting a price in advance. This prohibition applies to all kinds of produce with fluctuating prices, except for small, insignificant items that people are not particular about pricing, such as a single loaf of bread a woman borrows from her friend — there the Sages were not stringent about the rabbinic interest prohibition. But if a large quantity of food items is lent at once, such as twenty flatbreads, this is already considered significant and should not be permitted.
takeaways: It is forbidden to lend a quantity of a product (like grain) in exchange for the same quantity back when the borrower has none of it and there is no fixed market price, since the price might rise before repayment.
The solution: fix the loan's monetary value in advance, and repay according to it if the price changes.
Lending small, insignificant items (like a single loaf) is permitted even without assessment, but a large quantity is already significant and forbidden.

paragraphs: Ha deamarnu en lilvat sea bisa im en lalloveh meoto hammin haynu davqa deen lo kelal abal im yesh lo dabar muat meoto hammin yakol lilvot alayv elep sein veyoter vaapillu chitta achat yakol lilvot aleha kamma sein lepi shekkol chitta shemmalveh lo roin keillu chitta zo niknesa tachteha lihyot birshut hammalveh ukeshennityaqqeru aach"k birshuto nityaqqeru ulepi zeh otam baale battim shelevin zeh mizzeh kikkerot lechem o mine mezonot harbeh sheasarnu leel hinneh im yesh lalloveh chittim bebeto veraq kikkarot apuyim en lo muttar lilvot kikkarot harbeh kaasher yirtzeh al semak otam hachittim sheyyesh lo bebeto ki hayyoqer vehazzol hu bechittim velo bekikkarot gupan.

clarification.explanation: The prohibition of lending se'ah for se'ah applies only when the borrower has none at all of that kind. But if he has even a very small amount of that kind, he may borrow a much larger quantity — even a loan based on a single grain of wheat he has at home permits him to borrow large quantities of wheat. The reason: any wheat he receives as a loan is considered as though it entered in place of the wheat he already has and becomes entirely his own, so if the price rises, this happens while it is already in his possession, and there is no interest here. From this a practical ruling follows: people who borrow loaves of bread or many food items from each other — which we forbade earlier when they have none at all — if they have wheat at home (even though they have no baked loaves), they may borrow as many loaves as they wish, since the price fluctuation is determined by the wheat's price, not by the loaves themselves.
takeaways: If the borrower has even a little of the kind in question — even a single grain — he may borrow a much larger quantity of it.
The reason: what he borrows is considered to enter in place of what he already has and becomes entirely his own.
One who has wheat at home may borrow many loaves of bread, since the price is set by the wheat, not the loaves.

paragraphs: Kol sheamarnu sheyyaspiq dabar muat lilvat alayv hu raq bederek halvaa abal bemeker la mehanne dabar muat ella im ken yesh lo keneged kol hammaot:

clarification.explanation: The leniency that a "small amount" of the kind suffices to permit a larger loan applies only to a loan. But when it concerns an actual sale — that is, the buyer pays now and the merchandise is delivered later — it does not suffice for the seller to have a "small amount" of that kind; rather he must have merchandise on hand equal to the entire sum he received.
takeaways: The "small amount" leniency applies only to a loan, not a sale.
In a sale, the seller must have merchandise on hand equal to the entire advance payment received.

paragraphs: Yesh sheshsholechim shuttapim o sheluchim besakar meqomot haarbiyyim liqnot mishsham tzemer vehem yoshebim beir bagdad ubaim etzel socher yisrael ulequchim mimmennu maot beiyyayr mea liro (shem matbea), al menat sheyyimkeru lo kenegdan tzemer sheyyebiuhu lo achar shene chodashim vinakku lo min erek hashshaar sheyyotze aach"k arbaa lemea asur ki zeh mechasser lo min erek hashshaar bishbil shemmaqdim lo hammaot qodem sheyyimsor lo hatztzemer bishne chodashim abal im zeh ba lo yedia mishshuttapo o shelucho hayyosheb etzel haarbiyyim shekkebar qana lo kak vekak sein shel tzemer vehem beyado veraq tzarik lahem zeman harbeh ad sheyyimtza lo sepina vegam zeman hadderek ulekak hu loqeach atta maot keneged oto hatztzemer min hattaggar bishbil ikkabt hazzeman ad sheyyaggia hatztzemer hu pochet lo meerek hashshaar kak vekak lemea let lan bah mippene shehatztzemer kebar qibbelu min haarbiyyim venaasa beyado veniqneh lalloqeach bemaot ellu vbsh"q mqbtzyl asiti open hetter limkor "p sheadayin lo qibbel shuttapo tzemer mearbiyyim velo qana kelum:

clarification.explanation: It was customary for partners or agents to be sent to Arab regions to buy wool, receiving an advance in cash from a Jewish merchant (for example, one hundred pounds), in exchange for delivering wool to him after two months, with the payment for that wool discounted slightly (for example, four pounds per hundred) because the payment was advanced. This is forbidden, since in practice the merchant receives less money for the waiting period — hidden interest on the cash advance. But if the agent already reported he actually bought a certain quantity of wool from the Arabs, and it is already in his possession, and he is now only waiting for the ship and transport time — it is permitted for the merchant to pay in advance with a certain discount for that waiting time, since the wool has already been actually purchased and is considered the buyer's property, and this is already an ordinary sale of existing merchandise, not an interest loan. In his book "Miqabtzeel" the Ben Ish Chai further found a way to permit selling this way even when the partner had not yet received the wool from the Arabs and had not bought anything.
takeaways: An advance to a merchant for wool to be delivered in two months, discounted from the rate — forbidden (hidden interest on the cash advance).
But if the wool was already actually purchased and is in the agent's hands, and the advance payment is only for the waiting time for transport — permitted (a sale of existing merchandise).
In Miqabtzeel, the Ben Ish Chai found a way to permit it even when the partner had not yet bought anything.

paragraphs: Yesh bene adam sheyyesh lahem zehubim verotzim lehachalipam bematbea kesep shehu ryy"l (yechidat matbea parsit) mgyd"y (yechidat matbea tureqit) vekayyotze umoserim mea zehubim lechelpan al menat sheyyabi lahem temuratam matbeot hakkesep achar t"v yom o sheloshim uposeqim immo erek hakkesep bepachot bishbil qedimat hammaot asur abal im yesh lechallapan matbeot kesep ellu bpvst" (doar) o bispina sheyyabou leyado achar t"v o esrim yom vehu moker otam bepachot kede sheyyeqabbel atta hazzehubim miyyad muttar ak kevan shehu derek meker tzarik sheyyihyeh lo kesep keneged kol hazzehubim shemmeqabbel: mihu ani omer hannohagim hetter bedabar zeh poh irenu lipsoq haerek shel matbeot hakkesep im hachalpan "p sheen lechallapan matbeot kesep beet shemmeqabbel hazzehubim en limchot beyadam deyesh lahem lismok al teshubat harashba" za"l shebbia mera"n za"l bebet yosep siman q"g vezeh leshono katab harashba" cheleq g' siman r"k reuben makar leshimon mea denerim brtzlvny" veku' im darkam lihyot lahem shaar arok hare hu asur abal im hashshaar mishtanneh tadir en zeh hashshaar qatzub veen bo mishshum ribbit ad kan leshono yeuyyan sham vehinneh poh irenu en lematbeot shaar arok ella mishtannim lipamim mishshabua leshabua umechodesh lachodesh velipamim miyyom leyom yishtanneh hashshaar velaken im zeh baal hazzehubim poseq im hachalpan erek matbea hakkesep bepachot mishshaar hashshuq o mesim erek hazzehubim shennoten beerek yoter mishshaar hashshuq hinneh epshar shebbeoto hayyom atzmo yishtanneh hashshaar shel zeh veshel zeh shehazzehubim yaalu meat vehakkesep yarad venimtza shello hirvicha kelum erek zeh sheppasaq immo:

clarification.explanation: One who has gold coins and wishes to exchange them for silver coins (such as a Persian real or a Turkish majidi), and hands the gold coins to a money changer so he will bring back silver coins in two weeks or a month — if a lower price for the silver is already set now because the payment is advanced, this is forbidden, since it is a loan and not an actual sale. But if the changer already actually has silver coins on the way (by post or ship) that will arrive in about two or three weeks, and sells them now at a discount to receive the gold immediately, this is permitted — since this concerns a sale of something already existing, provided the changer has cash on hand equal to the entire sum of gold he receives. The Ben Ish Chai adds that the widespread custom in his city to permit setting the price even when the changer does not yet actually have the silver coins should not be protested against, since one may rely on the Rashba's approach: a fixed, long-term price set in advance at a discount is forbidden, but a price that fluctuates frequently (like the coins in that city, whose price changes from week to week and even day to day) is not considered a "fixed rate" and carries no interest prohibition, since there is no certainty the price will specifically rise.
takeaways: It is forbidden to fix in advance a discounted price for future currency exchange not yet actually held by the changer — hidden interest.
If the changer already has actual coins on the way, it is permitted to sell them now at a discount, provided he has cash on hand equal to the full sum.
When a currency's price fluctuates frequently (not a fixed rate), one may be lenient, since there is no certainty of a rise — and the local custom of leniency has grounds to rely upon.

paragraphs: Reuben yesh lo chob al shimon mea zehubim ukeshehiggia zeman piron hachob veamar lo: "ten li hammea zehubim, sheani rotzeh liqnot bahem matbeot kesep, shetztzarik li leshallecham bashshabua habba bispina" veamar lo shimon "aseh otam alay matbeot kesep sheatta rotzeh, vaani abiem leka bashshabua habba" - "p shechoshebin hazzehubim vehakkesapim kepi erek sheshshavim beoto hayyom shettaba oto, hinneh im bashshabua habba keshemmoser lo hakkesapim nityaqqer hashshaar shellahem asur, yaan ki zeh lo haya lo maot oto hayyom sheppasaq immo haerek kede shennomar dahava epshar liqnot bahem matbeot ellu ella zeh asa otam alayv kechob shehaya chayyab lo velaken im nityaqqeru asur lachshob otam keerek hazzol sheppasaq immo:

clarification.explanation: If Shimon owes Reuven one hundred gold coins and the repayment date arrived, and Reuven requested that instead of receiving gold coins, Shimon pay him silver coins in the future (which he needs to send by ship), and Shimon agreed to fix now how much the silver is worth at today's price — even though at the time of fixing the prices are exactly equal, if a week later when the silver is actually delivered its price has risen, it is forbidden to calculate it at the old, cheaper price. The reason: unlike the money changer in the previous case, here Shimon did not actually have cash at that moment to buy the silver coins with — he merely "created them upon himself" as a debt, and this is therefore actually a loan, not a sale, and any price rise at repayment time is forbidden interest.
takeaways: The distinction between a loan and a sale depends on whether the paying party actually had cash on hand at the time of fixing the price.
When there is no actual cash, only an obligation (debt), a price rise at repayment time is forbidden as interest, even if the prices were equal at the original fixing.

paragraphs: Haolam nohagin poh irenu y" lilvot matbea bematbea dehaynu lava mimmennu mea leyare hayyom umeshallem lo mea liro achar chodesh veken bematbeot kesep v"p shebbeet happeraon mityaqqer hashshaar shel halyare. veen chosheshin ledaqdeq sheyyihyeh lalloveh matbea echad meoto hammin amenam harab chakemat adam za"l ql"b seip t' katab shetztzarik lihyot lalloveh matbea meoto hammin veayyen bebinat adam siman g' veayyen chakemat adam siman qs"b babbeurim seip qatan d' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: It was customary in the Ben Ish Chai's city to borrow one type of coin (such as a lira) in exchange for the same coin — for example, borrowing one hundred lira today and returning one hundred lira in a month — even though in the meantime the lira's rate (value) might rise. No care was taken that the borrower have a coin of that exact kind at the time of the loan, unlike the law of "se'ah for se'ah" mentioned above. The Ben Ish Chai notes that Rabbi Chochmat Adam wrote that indeed the borrower must have a coin of that kind, and refers to additional books (Binat Adam, Chochmat Adam) for further study on this.
takeaways: The local custom was to be lenient in lending one coin for the same coin even without the borrower already having a coin of that kind, unlike lending grain.
Some are stricter (Rabbi Chochmat Adam), requiring that with coins too the borrower already have some of that kind from the outset, discussed further in additional sources.

paragraphs: Reuben toshab bagdad amar leshimon tabi sechora peloni millonedon vaani eqneh otah mimmeka berivvach esrim lemea vehammaot etten leka achar shettimsor li hassechora bishne chodashim o yoter hinneh zeh hammiqqach qorin oto bearbi mrbch"h (ashray temurat revach bischora) vehu muttar ubilbad shettihyeh hassechora ad sheyyimserenna liruben al shimon hammakur veayyen mhrshd"m yoreh dea siman s" velechem rab siman y"d ukeneset haggedola siman q"g haggahat hattur ot d' veod acharonim mihu aremat hachapatzim asura:

clarification.explanation: If Reuven asks Shimon to bring certain merchandise from London, and commits to buying it from him at a fixed profit margin (for example, twenty percent), with payment given only after the merchandise is delivered to him in two months or more — such a transaction, called in Arabic "murabaha" (a credit sale with fixed profit), is permitted. The central condition: the merchandise must already be Shimon's property at the time he sells it to Reuven, that is, this is a genuine sale of existing merchandise, not a transfer of money against future merchandise. The Ben Ish Chai adds that one must be careful of "a pile of objects" — that is, an artificial transaction disguised as a sale of objects but which is actually concealed interest lending — and this is forbidden.
takeaways: Selling existing merchandise on credit with a fixed profit (murabaha) is permitted, provided the merchandise is already actually the seller's at the time of sale.
One must be careful of artificial transactions ("a pile of objects") that attempt to disguise an interest loan as a sale of objects — this is forbidden.

paragraphs: Reuben chayyab leshimon mea zehubim lizman shelosha chodashim veamar reuben lelevi he leka tishim vesheba zehubim maot medudim akshav veatta teshallem hachob leshimon bizmanno hare zeh asur deellu hattishim vesheba zehubim shennoten lalloveh hem malveh venimtza loveh levi mereuben tishim vesheba uporea baado mea vahare zo ribbit gemura v"p shch"k levi piyyes et shimon velo natan lo ella tishim vesheba asur kevan diruben chayyab mea leshimon vezeh levi petaro mishshelosha bishbil shehilvahu tishim vesheba nimtza levi hanehu liruben biptur zeh ukeillu natan lo hashshelosha ukemo shekkatab beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman seip n"ch yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: Reuven owes Shimon one hundred gold coins, payable in three months. If Reuven gives Levi ninety-seven gold coins in cash now, so Levi will pay Shimon the full one hundred in his place when the time arrives — this is forbidden, since in practice Levi borrowed ninety-seven from Reuven and committed to pay one hundred in his place, which is full-fledged interest. Even if Levi ultimately succeeds in persuading Shimon to settle for only ninety-seven, it is still forbidden, since Reuven originally owed one hundred, and Levi "benefited" Reuven by releasing him from three gold coins in exchange for this loan — which is itself hidden interest.
takeaways: It is forbidden to accept a reduced sum in cash now in exchange for a commitment to pay the full original sum at a later date — this is full-fledged interest.
Even if in practice less than the original debt was ultimately paid, the prohibition still stands, since the very benefit from the time difference is the interest.

paragraphs: Hammalveh maneh lachabero al menat sheyyitten dinar leadam acher "p sheen hammalveh haya chayyab litten haddinar leoto adam vaapillu sheamar lo sheyyitten haddinar litzdaqa hare zeh asur dachashib keillu natan haddinar lammalveh atzmo vaapillu shehammalveh lo amar lo kelum ella halloveh amar tilloni maneh vaani etten dinar litzdaqa o liploni vehilvahu bistam bishbil kak asur:

clarification.explanation: One who lends money to his fellow on condition that the borrower give a coin to a third party — even if the lender himself owed nothing at all to that third party, and even if he asked that the coin be given to charity — this is forbidden, since it is considered as though the coin was given to the lender himself, and this is an addition for the loan. Even if the lender requested nothing, but the borrower himself proposed "lend me a maneh and I will give a coin to charity or to so-and-so," and the loan was given based on this — it is still forbidden.
takeaways: It is forbidden to condition a loan on the borrower giving payment or a donation to a third party, even to charity — this is hidden interest.
Even if the idea for this condition came from the borrower himself rather than the lender, the prohibition still stands.

paragraphs: Reuben qana sechora min haggoy bemea lizman y"b chodesh veasa haggoy tenay im reuben sheyyabiu lo hammaot achar shene chodashim vinakkeh lo asara lemea bishbil haasara chodashim vehinneh achar b' chodashim taba haggoy et reuben sheyyabi hammaot kepi hattenay velo haya liruben maot asur leshimon litten hatteshii laggoy vehu yeqabbel hammea deme hammiqqach mereuben achar y"b chodashim:

clarification.explanation: Reuven bought merchandise from a gentile for one hundred gold coins, payable in twelve months, and the gentile agreed that if Reuven pays already after two months, he would receive a ten-percent discount for the remaining ten months. When the two-month date arrived and Reuven had no money to pay, it is forbidden for Shimon to pay the discounted ninety on his behalf to the gentile, and in exchange receive the full one hundred from Reuven after twelve months — since here Shimon is effectively lending Reuven ninety and receiving back one hundred, which is interest.
takeaways: It is forbidden for a third party to pay a discounted sum on the borrower's behalf, and in exchange collect the full sum from the borrower at a later date — this is a full-fledged interest loan.

paragraphs: Reuben tzarik lemaot yesh taqqana sheyyelek etzel shimon veyiktob lo shimon shetar chob sheqqorin kmbyyl"h shehu modeh shechayyab lipquddat reuben sak mea zehubim lizman kak vekak. veyiktob shemmaot ellu higgiu lo min reuben medudim o higgiu lo becheshbon o hem deme sechora veyiktob gam ken shem hair shehu koteb vechotem bah kede sheyyihyeh lishtar zeh koach shetarot sheqqure kmbyylh kede sheyyukal reuben limkor shetar zeh laacherim al yede ketiba shel giro. sheal yede kak yimkor reuben shetar kimbayyala zeh lihuda bepachot viqabbel hammaot ubizman happeraon yeqabbel yehuda min shimon mea bishtar zeh shebbeyado veshimon yeqabbel mereuben et mea ellu shennatan lihuda sheyyesh hetter laasot beopen zeh veraq yehuda asur leqabbel shum dinar min reuben velo yihyeh lo eseq immo bedabar zeh kelal v"p debeemet shimon lo haya chayyab liruben kelum beet shekkatab shetar zeh yukal haadam lechayyeb atzmo behodaato "p shehi sheqer v"g dibdin yisrael en qoneh yehuda shetar kimbayyala zeh biktiba zo shel giro shekkatab reuben mikkol maqom kevan deqoneh hu bedina sheyyihyeh shetar zeh metuqqan kepi dina demalkuta keminhag hassocharim dehaynu shekkatub shimon shehu mitchayyeb lipquddat reuben vegam koteb shem hair shehu koteb vechotem bah vegam yiktob shehassak hazzeh shehu mitchayyeb bo higgia leyado bimzumman o becheshbon o deme sechora ki raq beopen zeh nechshab bedina demalkuta kimbayyala shehu niqneh leacher biktiba zo shel haggiru shekkoteb reuben al gup hashshetar debarim ellu: "veanena tidpa sak veku' lemor yehuda veku' " vekaasher katabnu leel: mihu im reuben veshimon shenehem tzerikim lemaot kol echad mea zehubim en yekolim laasot open tiqqun zeh sheyyiktob shimon kimbayla leshem reuben bematayim veyimkor reuben shetar zeh lihuda bepachot veyabi hachetzi leshimon vehachetzi yiqqach leatzmo ubizman happeraon yeqabbel yehuda hammatayim mishshimon veshimon yeqabbel hammea min reuben dedabar zeh asur mishshum sheyyesh besak zeh mea deshayeki leshimon dipchat shellahem napeq minneh vehu musar mea meshallem lihuda ukemo shekkatab bequnteres hsm" shebbesop seper mizbach adama yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation:
For Reuven who needs cash — there is a remedy (to bypass the interest prohibition): he goes to Shimon, and Shimon writes him a promissory note ("kambiyala," a commercial note) in which he acknowledges owing to Reuven's order one hundred gold coins at a certain time, and writes that the money reached him from Reuven (as a loan, an accounting balance, or merchandise payment), and the name of the city where he wrote and signed it — so the note has the validity of a commercial note transferable to others by endorsement ("giro"). This way Reuven can sell the note to Yehuda for less and receive cash immediately; at repayment time, Yehuda will receive one hundred from Shimon, and Shimon will receive the one hundred from Reuven. This is permitted — only Yehuda may not receive anything from Reuven or deal with him at all. And although in truth Shimon owed Reuven nothing, a person can obligate himself by his own acknowledgment even if false; and although under Jewish law Yehuda does not acquire it through the endorsement, he nevertheless acquires it under the law of the land (as merchant custom), when the note is properly drawn up (city name, the wording "to Reuven's order," and that the sum reached him in cash/accounting/merchandise payment).

But if both Reuven and Shimon need cash (each one hundred) — they cannot perform this remedy (having Shimon write a kambiyala for two hundred, Reuven selling it for less, bringing half to Shimon and keeping half) — since this is forbidden, because one hundred of the sum belongs to Shimon, and the loss from the discounted sale comes out of his share (Sma).
takeaways: A remedy for Reuven needing cash: Shimon writes him a promissory note (kambiyala) acknowledging he owes him money to his order, and Reuven sells it to Yehuda for less and receives cash — permitted (Yehuda must not deal with Reuven).
The note is acquired by force of the law of the land when drawn up per merchant custom (city name, "to Reuven's order," and that the sum reached him).
If Shimon also needs cash, this cannot be done for the shared sum, since the discount loss would come out of his share.

paragraphs: Yisrael shellava mehaggoy asur leyisrael lihyot areb dehaggoy tobea heareb abal im lava yisrael miggoy lizman shishsha chodashim venatan halvaa sak haribbit kullo laggoy tekep umiyyad muttar leyisrael lihyot areb bishbil haqqeren bilbad veken reuben veshimon shetztzarik lekol echad mea zehubim ulevu otam mehaggoy beyachad asur liktob velachtom bishtar echad al hammatayim zehubim beyachad "p shello katebu ratza mizzeh gobeh lepi shebbedina demalkuta beminhag hassocharim nitchayyebu shenehem bematayim sheim yirtzeh haggoy litboa kol hammatayim meechad mehem yakol al ken tzarik shekkol echad yiktob shetar bipne atzmo al mea shello veim pareu laggoy et haribbit kullo miyyad velo nisharu chayyabim lo ella bead haqqeren bilbad yekolim litten shenehem shetar echad bematayim:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for a Jew to guarantee for another Jew who borrowed from a gentile with interest, since if the borrower does not pay, the gentile will collect the interest from the guarantor, and the guarantor Jew would thereby end up paying interest himself. But if the Jew borrowed from the gentile for a certain term (for example, six months) and immediately paid the gentile all the interest in advance, so that only the principal remains owed, another Jew may guarantee for the principal alone. Likewise, if two people (Reuven and Shimon) each need one hundred gold coins and borrowed them together from a gentile, they may not sign one joint note for two hundred, since under the law of the land and merchant custom, each of them becomes a guarantor for the entire sum, which is like guaranteeing interest for one's fellow. Therefore each must write a separate note for his own debt. If the entire interest was already paid to the gentile immediately, leaving only the principal, they may write one joint note.
takeaways: It is forbidden to guarantee for one who borrowed from a gentile with interest, since the guarantor might be required to pay the interest himself.
If the interest was paid to the gentile in advance, leaving only the principal, guaranteeing is permitted.
Two borrowers receiving a joint gentile loan must sign separate notes, unless all the interest was already paid in advance.

paragraphs: Shuttapim shellava echad mehem maot beribbit min haggoy letzorek hashshuttaput venoten et haribbit min haemtza yesh omerim deeno muttar ella im ken haya rivvach min hammaot haelleh shellava sheaz yittol haribbit techilla min harivvach vehashshear yachaloqu veyesh mattirim liqqach haribbit miqqeren hashshuttaput "p shello haya rivvach vetzarik lachush lisbarat haoserin veyaasu tiqqun lazeh kak dehashshuttap kol paam sheyyiqqach min haggoy beribbit letzorek eseq hashshuttaput yeshallem laggoy et haribbit miyyad min mamon hashshuttaput velo yishshaer chayyab laggoy ella raq haqqeren bilbad veim nizdammen shehu laqach mea dinarim lizman shishsha chodashim sheoleh haribbit shellahem shishsha dinarim venatan otam laggoy tekep mimmeot hashshuttaput qodem shemmeqabbel mimmennu hammea dinarim veachar shehiggia zeman happeraon lo haya yakol liproa haqqeren laggoy verotzeh sheyyamtin lo od shelosha chodashim ulechaddesh lo shetar chadash gam bazeh yaaseh kak yiqqach haribbit mikkis hashshuttaput shel shelosha chodashim habbaim veyittenem laggoy qodem sheyyaggia zeman happeraon beyom echad veachar sheyyaggia zeman happeraon shel shetar hayyashan vekoteb lo shetar chadash kebar natan haribbit mikkis hashshuttaput shehem kemo mattana laggoy ki adayin lo nitchayyeb lo ribbit baabur shelosha chodashim habbaim veken al zo hadderek laasot bekol paam sheyyirtzeh: veken name hainyan biruben toshab bagdad koteb leshimon toshab lonedon sheyyiqqach lo maot beribbit min haggoy kede liqnot lo bahem sechora degam ken yaaseh kak sheyyitten reuben reshut leshimon latet laggoy haribbit haoleh lo bishbil kamma chodashim bimzumman min mamon shello sheyyesh lo beyado veaz nimtza shimon eno areb laggoy ella bead haqqeren ki haribbit natan laggoy min mamon reuben birshuto ubishlichuto qodem shehu naasa areb laggoy veoto haribbit hu naasa betorat mattana mereuben legoy al yede shimon veen bazeh chashash kelal vetiqqun zeh leshallem haribbit min mamon halloveh battechilla ketabo mahara"sh abbuhab za"l beseper hazzikronot vehebio hakkeneset haggedola siman qs"ch haggahat hattur ot b' yeuyyan sham veayyen mah shekkatabti bs"d bsh"q rab berakot dap ql"ch yeuyyan sham ubeemet hu tiqqun amitti ubarur kevan diruben marsheh leshimon latet laggoy mehammamon sheyyesh lo beyado have lah marshehu latet mattana laggoy vezeh shimon hu noten deme haribbit veaach"k meqabbel hammaot min haggoy veen bazeh shum chashash velaken "p sheharab pene mosheh cheleq b' siman tz"b, asa tiqqun acher shezzeh shimon yiqqach hammaot beribbit min haggoy leatzmo veyiqneh bahem sechora leatzmo, veaach"k yaabir hassechora liruben berivvach kepi haribbit shemmasar laggoy bead hammaot hahem yeuyyan sham hinneh apillu im nannicha bemunnach sheen lepaqpeq bazeh haopen kelum im kol zeh, taqqana hannizkeret leel adipa, yaan deepshar sheyyizdammen shehiggia zeman happeraon velo shalach reuben haddamim veatta mah yaaseh shimon? ki haggoy chosheb alayv ribbit massa umattan veek yiqqach haribbit mereuben? ak badderek shekkatabti yabo nakon ki reuben yishlach leshimon sak muat keneged haribbit veyitten lo reshut latet mizzeh hammamon ribbit laggoy qodem sheyyaggia zeman happeraon venimtza mah shechozer veloveh mechadash achar halvaa rishona kebar para ribbit shellah mimmamon reuben:

clarification.explanation: Partners where one of them borrowed money with interest from a gentile for the partnership's needs and pays the interest from the shared fund — some say this should not be permitted unless there was profit from the money (in which case he takes the interest first from the profit and the rest is divided), and some permit taking the interest from the partnership's principal even without profit. One should be concerned for the forbidding view, and adopt a remedy: whenever the partner borrows from the gentile with interest for the partnership's needs, he should pay the gentile the interest immediately from the partnership funds, so only the principal remains owed to the gentile. Likewise, if the repayment time arrives and he cannot pay, and wishes to renew the note for an additional term, he should give the gentile the next period's interest from the partnership fund a day before the repayment date (as a gift, before he becomes obligated in it). Likewise, if Reuven (in Baghdad) writes to Shimon (in London) to borrow with interest on his behalf to buy merchandise, Reuven should give Shimon permission to pay the gentile the interest from Reuven's own money in his hands, so Shimon guarantees only the principal, and the interest is given as a gift from Reuven to the gentile. This remedy (paying the interest from the borrower's own funds in advance) is a genuine remedy (Maharash Avuhav, Knesset HaGedolah), and is preferable to another remedy (of "Pnei Moshe," that Shimon borrow for himself and transfer the merchandise to Reuven at a profit equal to the interest rate).
takeaways: A partner who borrowed from a gentile with interest for the partnership and pays interest from the fund — disputed whether permitted without profit; one should be concerned for the forbidding view.
The remedy: pay the gentile's interest immediately from the partnership funds (or in advance, before renewing the note), leaving only the principal owed.
Likewise in an inter-city loan: the principal party pays the interest from his own money as a gift to the gentile — no concern, and this is preferable to the "Pnei Moshe" remedy.

paragraphs: Reuben natan maot leshimon lehitasseq machatzit sakar vezeh reuben lava maot minnakeri beribbit unetanan leshimon lehitasseq bahem eno rashshay reuben lachshob lo haribbit lehepsed linkuto min harivvach veayyen beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman seip d':

clarification.explanation: If Reuven gives Shimon money for business at half-profit ("iska"), and Reuven himself borrowed this money from a gentile with interest — Reuven may not count the interest he paid the gentile as a business loss and deduct it from the profit shared with Shimon, since the interest is Reuven's personal obligation, not the partnership's.
takeaways: It is forbidden to roll the interest Reuven paid on his personal gentile loan into the half-profit partnership as a business loss — it is Reuven's personal burden alone.

paragraphs: Reuben sheasa leshimon shalicha liqnot lo sechorot lizman min haggoyim beyoter ulemakeram lo bepachot bemaot medudim "p sheshshimon natan deme hassechora hahi shemmekarah bepachot liruben ukeshehiggia zeman happeraon shellah laqach dameha mereuben venimtza natan liruben tishim veqibbel mimmennu achar zeh mea muttar vekol shekken im zeh shimon, achar shemmakar otah sechora bepachot lo natan haddamim liruben ella qana lo bahem sechora demuttar vehattaam mippene ki shimon qana hassechora bishlichut reuben umekarah gam ken bishlichut reuben venimtza hammiqqach hu shel reuben ukeillu reuben qana min haggoy ureuben makar vaapillu bedabar sheshshumato yedua yesh lehaqel dekevan demidderabbanan hu deasur miyyisrael leyisrael lehaki beqoneh min haggoy bishlichuto bikhay gavna la ashkachna digzur kak katab haggaon morenu rabbi yaaqob qshtrv behaggahotayv vehebi haggaon chida" za"l beshiyyure beraka siman qs"t ot va"v umashma middebarayv dibdabar sheen shumato yedua apillu liqnot lo miyyisrael shari bikhay gavna:

clarification.explanation: If Reuven appointed Shimon as his agent to buy merchandise from gentiles at a high price and sell it at a lower cash price, and Shimon paid the proceeds from the sale (for example, ninety) to Reuven, and then at the repayment date received back from him (for example, one hundred) — this is permitted. And all the more so if Shimon, after selling the merchandise for less, did not give the money to Reuven but bought him other merchandise with it — this too is permitted. The reason: Shimon acted as Reuven's agent in both the buying and selling, so the entire transaction is considered as though Reuven himself bought from the gentile and sold, not as a loan between two Jews. Even in a case where the merchandise has a fixed, known price, one should be lenient, since the interest prohibition between Jews is generally rabbinic, and when the purchase is made through agency vis-à-vis a gentile, we do not find that the Sages decreed against this. And in cases where the merchandise has no fixed, known price, one should be even more lenient — to the point that it is even permitted to acquire this way even from a Jew, not only from a gentile.
takeaways: When a person acts as an agent in both buying and selling on his fellow's behalf, the price gap is considered part of the principal's transaction, not an interest loan.
For an item with no fixed, known price, one should be even more lenient about this.

paragraphs: Yisrael shennatan maot lenakeri beisqa lehitasseq bahem lemachatzit sakar vehilva hannakeri min maot ellu leyisreelim beribbit "p sheyyisrael baal hammaot yodea bekak shari kevan dehane zuze mishtabedi lenakeri hamqabbel lemachatzit sakar apillu ki yada la matze meakkeb beyad hannakeri millehalvot shehu rotzeh lehistakker baasher yimmatze veki qaabid addata denapsheh qaabid, ken katab mhrym"t za"l besiman qy"v, vekatab shehu haddin beshuttaput im haheqdesh yeuyyan sham. vehaggaon chiqre leb za"l beyoreh dea cheleq b' siman tv"b heerik beinyan zeh lebarer haddin beshuttaput haggoy ubedap l"b ammud d' hebi dibre haggaon mhrym"t za"l hannizkar ak bedap l"g ammud b' rapya bideh shekkatab: lehaqel beshel tora tzerika rabba yeuyyan sham veayyen binyan tziyyon siman s"h mah shekkatab beinyan zeh yeuyyan sham al ken rauy lachush beheka dehaggoy noten beribbit qetzutza deasur min hattora abal im haggoy natan leyisrael beribbit derabbanan yesh lismok lehattir:

clarification.explanation: If a Jew gave money to a gentile in an "iska" (half-profit) transaction, and the gentile lent part of this money with interest to other Jews — even though the owner of the money (the Jew) knows about this, it is permitted, since the money is already considered pledged to the gentile receiving it for the transaction, and he may do with it as he wishes to profit, while the Jewish money owner cannot prevent this. This is likewise true in a partnership with a "hekdesh" (consecrated property). Nevertheless, the Ben Ish Chai adds that one should be careful in a case where the loan the gentile gives is "fixed interest" (defined and Torah-forbidden interest), and only when it concerns interest forbidden merely rabbinically should one be lenient and rely on the lenient approach.
takeaways: Money given to a gentile in a half-profit transaction is considered pledged to him, so if he lends it onward with interest, the Jewish money owner is not culpable, even knowing about it.
One should be more careful when the gentile's loan is Torah-forbidden interest, being lenient only for rabbinically forbidden interest.

paragraphs: Hannoten isqa lachabero dehaynu shennoten lo maot o sechora lehitasseq bahem lemachatzit sakar tzarik shettihyeh achrayut hazzol vaonasin shel chatzi haisqa al hannoten yaan ki kol isqa hachetzi shellah hu betorat halvaa lamqabbel shehare chatzi harivvach hu shello vehachetzi hashsheni shel haisqa hu piqqadon etzel hamqabbel shehare chatzi harivvach hu lannoten, lepikak tzarik lepachot sheyyihyeh achrayut hazzol vaonasin shel hachetzi shehu betorat piqqadon al noten abal acharayut shel geneba vaabeda im yihyeh hakkol al hamqabbel let lan bah mippene shehu keshomer sakar alayv shetztzarik latet hannoten lehamqabbel sekar tarecho baabur tirchato shettoreach bachatzi haisqa shehu betorat piqqadon beyado sheim lo yitten lo shetar tarecho, nimtza hu toreach bishbil hannoten baabur chatzi hashsheni shehilvahu vahare zeh abaq ribbit ak saggi latet lo sekar tarecho dabar muat kevan shehu matneh immo dabar muat mittechilla qodem shennatan lo hammaot venitratztza bekak vehaadam yukal lezalzel biskar tarecho kepi mah sheyyirtzeh veraq shello yipchot mishshiur dinar echad lekol yeme hashshuttaput vekatab haggaon shiyyure beraka za"l shiur dinar zeh hu y"b pura (matbea tureqi qatan) bizman sheshshaveh kesep mezuqqaq haddirham (yechidat mishqal = 3.2 garam) bishmona pura veal zo hadderek bishar meqomot lepi hammatbea veshivvuy hakkesep yeuyyan sham veim kebar natan lo maot haisqa velo pasaq immo bedabar muat baabur sekar tarecho lo yukal aach"k lipsoq bedabar muat ella yitten lo shene shelishe harivvach veim yihyeh hepsed lo yeqabbel raq chatzi hahepsed venimtza lepi zeh, chatzi shelish rivvach haodep lamqabbel hu biskar amalo veim achar sheyyada haddin rotzeh laasot tenay sekar tircha mikkan ulehabba tzarik sheyyebattel haeseq veyiqqach zeh et maot haisqa veyachazor vichaddesh otah mechadash sheyyatneh immo al sekar tarecho bedabar muat veyitten umeot haisqa lehitasseq bahem lemachatzit sakar kannizkar leel: veha debaenan sheyyaqtzib lammitasseq sekar tarecho haynu davqa im hamqabbel lebaddo hu oseq bemassa umattan shel maot ellu abal im gam hannoten oseq vetoreach immo beeseq "p shehamqabbel toreach yoter let lan bah veen tzarik liqtzotz lo sekar tarecho mihu tzarik sheyyihyeh dabar zeh meporash benehem mittechilla lehatnot sheyyihyeh baal hammaot gam ken kimchuyyab laasoq bemassa umattan shel haisqa hahi ukemo shekkatabti besipri mqbtzyl:

clarification.explanation: One who gives an "iska" to his fellow — that is, money or merchandise to trade with in exchange for half the profit — must ensure that responsibility for a price decline ("loss") and unforeseen events ("force majeure"), regarding half the money, falls on the one who gives the iska, not on the one managing it. The reason: halachically, half the transaction is considered a loan to the recipient (so his profit is his own and he bears the risk), and the other half is considered a deposit in the recipient's hands (whose profit belongs to the giver, and therefore the risk of price decline and force majeure also remains with the giver). By contrast, responsibility for theft and loss can fall entirely on the recipient, since he is considered a paid bailee, but he must be given payment for his effort in managing the deposit portion, since otherwise the effort he expends on the giver's portion is considered hidden interest ("dust of interest"). It suffices to give him a small management fee, provided this was agreed upon in advance before the money was handed over, and it is not less than a minimal value (the measure of one dinar for the entire partnership period). If the money was already handed over without fixing a management fee in advance, this cannot be remedied after the fact with a small sum; rather the recipient receives two-thirds of the profit (instead of half) and only half the loss — the difference being effectively his management fee. One who wishes to fix this after the transaction has already begun must cancel it and reopen it with an agreed management-fee condition. All this is true only when the recipient alone manages the money; if the giver also actively participates in the business (even though the recipient works harder), there is no need to fix him a management fee — provided this was explicitly agreed upon in advance.
takeaways: In a half-profit "iska" transaction, responsibility for price decline and force majeure regarding the "deposit" portion remains with the money giver, not the recipient.
The recipient managing the money alone must be given a small management fee in advance, or a hidden-interest problem arises.
If no management fee was fixed in advance, it can only be remedied through unequal profit/loss division (two-thirds profit, half loss) or opening a new transaction with an explicit condition.

paragraphs: Yesh notenim lebaal hachanut sheqqorin bezaez (mischar arigim) meilim ushear ashray lemakeram bachanuto vesam alehem erek umah sheyyimkor baal hachanut yoter mizzeh haerek, yihyeh hayyitron chatzi lebaal hachanut vachay lebaal haashray hinneh kevan shezzeh baal hachanut eno mechuyyab kelum beshum nezeq veim lo nimkeru beoto haerek vehukrach limkor bepachot en baal hachanut meshallem kelum en lazeh din isqa shetztzarik liqtzotz lo sekar tarecho ki zeh harivvach sheyyizdammen lo limkor yoter meoto erek zehu sekar tarecho ken heeleti bs"d bsh"q mqbtzyl upashut:

clarification.explanation: Textile shop owners ("bazzaz") were given garments and other credit goods for sale in their shop, with a base price fixed for them, such that whatever he sells above that price, the profit is divided between the shop owner and the credit provider. Since the shop owner bears no responsibility for any loss — if the goods did not sell at the fixed price and he was forced to sell for less, he pays nothing for this — this is not the law of an "iska" requiring a fixed management fee, since the profit he may receive on sales above the fixed price is itself his natural management fee, requiring no additional special arrangement.
takeaways: A commission-sale arrangement where the shop owner bears no risk at all is not considered an "iska" and requires no separate management fee — the profit above the base price is already his fee.
